item.text:
**7B.2 — Research Note**
Verdict: mixed, leaning no. I found some real corrective actions, but the larger 2024 record is stronger on suppression of scrutiny than on candid self-correction.

**Positive / corrective evidence**
- **[Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says](https://kelo.com/2024/03/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says/)** | Reuters via Kelo | 2024-03-28 | Claim: after six High Court judges alleged ISI intimidation, the Sharif government agreed to set up an inquiry commission. That is a meaningful response to a potentially damaging truth claim, not an immediate shutdown of it. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[PM orders action over ‘ineffective’ track, trace system](https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117)** | Dawn | 2024-05-08 | Claim: Sharif ordered action after an inquiry report found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective. This is one of the clearest examples of admitting a system failure and acting on it. | IDs: 7B.2
- **[Bisham attack: PM Shehbaz orders immediate action against 5 officials for negligence of duty](https://www.dawn.com/news/1826071/bisham-attack-pm-shehbaz-orders-immediate-action-against-5-officials-for-negligence-of-duty)** | Dawn | 2024-04-06 | Claim: after an inquiry report on the Bisham attack, Sharif ordered disciplinary action against five officials for negligence. That supports limited willingness to accept adverse findings and correct course. | IDs: 7B.2
- **[PM orders urgent inquiry into Neelum-Jhelum project’s technical fault](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-orders-urgent-inquiry-into-neelum-jhelum-projects-technical-fault/)** | APP | 2024-05-16 | Claim: Sharif ordered an urgent probe into the technical fault at Neelum-Jhelum. This looks like a fact-finding response to failure rather than denial or narrative management. | IDs: 7B.2
- **[Shehbaz takes U-turn on ‘military’s darling’ claim](https://www.dawn.com/news/1810208/shehbaz-takes-u-turn-on-militarys-darling-claim)** | Dawn | 2024-02-01 | Claim: Sharif reversed an earlier public boast about being the establishment’s “darling” and reframed the issue when challenged. This is at best a rhetorical correction, not a clean admission of error. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1

**Negative / misleading or punitive evidence**
- **[Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313)** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | Claim: the interior ministry confirmed X was blocked around the election period on national-security grounds. That directly restricted reporting and public monitoring at a politically sensitive moment. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[U.S. urges Pakistan to lift internet shutdowns, social media restrictions](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-urges-pakistan-to-lift-internet-shutdowns-social-media-restrictions-3310177)** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-21 | Claim: the U.S. State Department publicly condemned internet shutdowns and social-media restrictions in Pakistan and urged restoration of access. This supports the view that the government was limiting truthful reporting rather than allowing it. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | Claim: HRW said the government increased pressure on media, opposition, and NGOs, producing self-censorship and fear. That is strong evidence against a truth-telling or truth-tolerating posture. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan: New Government Cracks Down on Free Expression](https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/01/16/pakistan-new-government-cracks-down-free-expression)** | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-16 | Claim: HRW’s 2024 retrospective says journalists faced intimidation, harassment, surveillance, and self-censorship throughout 2024, while X was intermittently blocked and activists were detained. Even though published in 2025, it is direct summary evidence about 2024 conduct. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan: Authorities Must Immediately Release Imran Khan From Arbitrary Detention](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa33/8507/2024/en/)** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | Claim: Amnesty said the legal system was weaponized to keep Imran Khan detained and out of politics. That is strong evidence of punishing an opponent rather than correcting abuses transparently. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan: New Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/)** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | Claim: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded powers to restrict gatherings. That points to suppression of dissent rather than truth-friendly governance. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan government intensifies crackdown on political dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent)** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against peaceful PTI protesters. This is direct evidence of punishing critics and suppressing public scrutiny. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan: Controversial Punjab Defamation Act signed into law](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-06-25/pakistan-controversial-punjab-defamation-act-signed-into-law)** | Library of Congress | 2024-06-25 / 2024-06-26 | Claim: the act created tribunal and platform-suspension powers that critics said could be weaponized against critics and media. That is strong evidence against allowing truthful reporting. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1
- **[Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps)** | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | Claim: the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid intimidation allegations. That cuts against truthful dealing with courts and independent fact-finding. | IDs: 7B.2, 7B.1

**Search gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 example of Sharif plainly saying, “I was wrong,” about one of his own major public claims.
- The best positive evidence is reactive: inquiries, discipline after reports, and some technical corrections.
- The best negative evidence is structural: media blocking, protest suppression, judicial pressure, and legal tools that chilled reporting.
